Character.Description: A highly competent, focused woman coder and systems thinker

Base.Name: Dark blazer
Base.Description: Professional dark blazer over tech-casual attire, sleeves pushed up

Cyan and magenta neon rim light from the room

NegativeConstraints: No green-on-black terminal, modern terminal interface, flat-panel display or lowercase CoCo glyphs.
No robots, brains, faces on machines, anthropomorphic algorithms or floating neural-network holograms.
No added title, slogan, captions, signage, brand logos unrelated to the referenced hardware, or decorative lettering.
No invented readable generated output, performance numbers, charts, model parameters or assembly listings.
No modern computer or gadget implying hidden training or inference; no smartwatch.
No imaginary hardware controls, physical levers, sliders or chip changes standing in for prompt, parameter count or training data.
Natural hands, plausible contact with the keyboard, no extra fingers; preserve the character identity from all three references.
Illustration, not documentary evidence of a particular measured run or a literal reconstruction of the exhibit.

ProductionNotes.Framing: True 16:9 landscape; keep face, hands, computer and active screen inside the central 80% of width. No panoramic multi-panel composition.
ProductionNotes.DisplayRequirement: BLACK or very dark green chunky uppercase low-resolution characters ON A SOLID BRIGHT GREEN background. The green active rectangle occupies 7/8 (87.5%) of the visible screen-glass width AND height, centered with a dark border 1/16 of the glass width at each side and 1/16 of its height at top and bottom. These proportions apply in the screen plane before perspective and CRT curvature. Green fills spaces and blank lines. The dark border is inside the glass, not the plastic bezel. Never bright green glyphs on a black terminal background.
AcceptanceChecks: Character matches all three portrait references.
Silver CoCo, cream keys, red key, dark surround and separate CRT are recognizable.
Black characters on solid green, including blank space.
Green active area covers seven-eighths of each screen dimension.
Main action is legible as a thumbnail.
Any readable output matches the cited source or a captured program frame exactly.
No fictitious settings, charts or mechanisms are presented as evidence.
ProductionNotes.ScreenReferenceStatus: Illustrative glyph detail is too small to convey readable output; no captured program frame is represented.
ProductionNotes.AltTextDraft: An illustration of a silver-haired woman using a worn silver Color Computer beside a black-on-green CRT, with fanfold printouts behind the keyboard.

Situation.Name: Completing a familiar slogan
Situation.Setting: The established night-time retro-computing workbench. Close, practical, green CRT illumination with restrained cyan and magenta rim light; warm worn wood and textured silver hardware.
Situation.Camera: Medium-wide three-quarter view from just behind the computer side of the table. Character at left, hands at the keyboard in the foreground, CRT to the right. Her face and the screen are both visible. Vary the angle from post three rather than repeating its pointing-at-a-printout pose.

CharacterPose.Expression: Watching the screen with relaxed concentration
CharacterPose.BodyPosition: Seated at the keyboard, turned slightly toward the CRT
CharacterPose.Gesture: One hand at the Enter key after selecting a prompt; the other rests naturally beside the keyboard. No pointing at imaginary controls.

Article.Name: CoCo and composite CRT
Article.Description: A worn silver 1981 Radio Shack Color Computer 1, dark keyboard surround, yellowed cream keys, red key and period badge, matched to the project photograph. A separate beige period composite CRT, matched to the monitor in the approved post-three banner. No generic beige computer, black replacement keys or flat panel. BLACK or very dark green chunky uppercase low-resolution characters ON A SOLID BRIGHT GREEN background. The green active rectangle occupies 7/8 (87.5%) of the visible screen-glass width AND height, centered with a dark border 1/16 of the glass width at each side and 1/16 of its height at top and bottom. These proportions apply in the screen plane before perspective and CRT curvature. Green fills spaces and blank lines. The dark border is inside the glass, not the plastic bezel. Never bright green glyphs on a black terminal background.
Article.Application: Primary interaction; screen visible at a gentle angle.

Article.Name: Marketing prompt demonstration
Article.Description: Use the actual prompt-completion display as the content reference. The documented pair is I ADORE followed by MY 64. Use a captured frame if readable screen content is included; otherwise make actual character detail too small to read. Do not invent a chat window, instruction box or an on-screen training control.
Article.Application: CRT content. The keyboard interaction, rather than a diagram of three levers, is the main scene.

Article.Name: Computer-name training-data sheets
Article.Description: Three modest fanfold sheets with lists of Apple, Commodore and Tandy computer names, referring to the fan-corpus comparison. Text is secondary and too small to read; no invented measurements or model diagrams.
Article.Application: At the back of the workbench, subordinate to the keyboard and screen. These are printed training-data records, not material automatically scanned by the CoCo.

Environment.Name: Workbench and cables
Environment.Description: Worn wooden bench, restrained period cabling, distant cyan/magenta lighting
Environment.Application: Quiet continuity with earlier banners; no extra monitors or piles of props.

KeyDetails: One main action: a prompt is selected and its completion appears. Do not portray training and prediction as the same operation.
This banner represents the prompt example. Model-size comparisons and the measured ordering effect remain in the article rather than being encoded as invented visual controls.

Amber may accent a paper edge or key reflection; do not introduce amber text or a modern selection widget into the authentic CoCo screen.
Use reference-specific silver hardware with cream keys, not the obsolete black-key wording in the earlier scene spec.
Situation.LightingFocus: Solid green CRT light across the hands and face; cyan/magenta rim light defines the silhouette. The screen and keyboard remain the brightest meaningful objects.

ArticleContext.Title: The prompt, the size, the training data
Themes: The prompt changes context without updating parameters.
Larger model designs change capacity and computation, without guaranteeing better completion metrics.
Training-data selection and order change output frequencies.
